query: How can Singapore Airlines improve its overall rating and recommendation rate, especially on flights where passengers do not recommend it (Recommended = no)?

per_column.name: crew_service_quality
per_column.rationale: Categorising crew service into attentive/mechanical/rude gives a strong axis to explain non-recommendations, directly relevant to service improvement. Most samples map well to text. However, the seats-dreadful review (which never mentions crew) was labelled 'inattentive_or_rude', an unwarranted inference, indicating some ungrounded values.

per_column.name: food_quality_issue_type
per_column.rationale: Distinguishing types of food problems (poor taste, special meal error, ran out) is a genuine actionable axis for improvement. Sampled values (praised where food praised, Unknown where silent) are sound readings of the text.

per_column.name: amenity_reduction_signal
per_column.rationale: A boolean flag for perceived cutbacks could add some leverage on decline complaints, but it is heavily skewed (833 false) and somewhat generic; its usefulness overlaps conceptually with perceived_service_decline. Sampled values are all plausibly grounded (false where no such signal).

per_column.name: cabin_class_value_gap
per_column.rationale: Flagging whether a class underdelivered relative to expectation is a valuable axis for value-for-money analysis and non-recommendation drivers. Mostly grounded, though 'economy_as_expected' is sometimes assigned to reviews that don't explicitly state class (e.g. Phuket seats review), a mild inference risk but generally defensible.

per_column.name: perceived_service_decline
per_column.rationale: Capturing whether a passenger perceives the airline declining is a meaningful signal for a premium carrier's reputation and recommendation. Somewhat overlaps with amenity_reduction_signal but adds a distinct sentiment-over-time angle. Sampled values grounded (false where no decline mentioned).

judge.rationale: The added columns provide several genuinely useful analytical axes (crew service quality, food issue typing, cabin-class value gap, perceived decline) that directly support diagnosing why passengers do not recommend Singapore Airlines and where to improve. Two boolean signals partially overlap but each still adds a distinct angle. Groundedness is high overall: silent rows are sensibly marked Unknown/false, and most produced values are sound readings of source text. The main weakness is occasional over-inference, notably labelling a crew-silent seat-comfort review as 'inattentive_or_rude', which slightly lowers groundedness.
